title: Cookie Monster gets last laugh at Elmo after Knicks clinch NBA championship
content:
Elmo couldn’t pick a side between the San Antonio Spurs and New York Knicks, but the Cookie Monster did. Now, he’s holding the trophy and taunting Elmo for his indecisiveness.

Just before the NBA Finals, Elmo, the famous Muppet from the children’s show “Sesame Street,” gave his best wishes on X to both the Knicks and the Spurs.

“Elmo hopes both teams have fun!”

That’s fine and all, except they don’t play both sides where Elmo’s from.

The Knicks went on to beat the Spurs in five games behind the play of NBA Finals MVP guard Jalen Brunson. Brunson scored 45 points as the Knicks closed out the Spurs Saturday night with a 94-90 win in San Antonio. He joins late Hall of Famer Willis Reed (1973, 1970) as the only players in franchise history to win NBA Finals MVP.

With the finals trophy in hand for the Knicks, the Cookie Monster didn’t forget Elmo’s flexible fandom Sunday morning.

The fictional Sesame Street is located in Manhattan. So when Elmo sent well-wishes to the Knicks’ finals opponent, thousands of New York fans were outraged, including the official New York City Department of Transportation, which sent a tweet jokingly threatening to take down the official Sesame Street sign located at the intersection of West 63rd Street and Broadway.

Widespread backlash was directed at Elmo, with taunts from fans and celebrities alike online. Former New York City Mayor Eric Adams responded with a “Bruh” GIF, while the Empire State Building’s account didn’t believe in Elmo’s fence-sitting.

“You picked the Knicks, let’s be for real, Elmo,” the account tweeted.

Elmo received so much backlash that he later responded to his own tweet with a correction and an attempt to reestablish his public loyalty.

“KNICKS that last message!” Elmo wrote. “Elmo didn’t mean to SPUR you on!”

The Cookie Monster has the trophy now, and he’s the one having fun.
